question: If a member is absent for a period of ____________ without permission, then the member's seat can be declared as "empty" by the House.  (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: 60 Days
120 Day
90 Day
30 Day
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 60 Days

Explanation:
According to Article 101(4) of the Indian Constitution, if a member of Parliament is absent from the House for a period of 60 consecutive days without the permission of the House, the House may declare the seat vacant. This provision applies to both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. The period of 60 days is counted from the day the member started being absent without permission. This rule is designed to prevent irregular attendance of members and ensure smooth functioning of parliamentary proceedings.

☛ Who has the authority to declare the seat vacant → The House
☛ This provision applies to → Both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
☛ When does the period of absence start counting → From the date of absence without permission
☛ Purpose of Article 101(4) → To regulate members' absenteeism
question_hi: यदि कोई सदस्य बिना अनुमति के ____________ अवधि तक अनुपस्थित रहता है, तो सदन द्वारा सदस्य की सीट को "रिक्त" घोषित किया जा सकता है। (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 2)

120 दिन
90 दिन
30 दिन
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 60 दिन

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 101(4) के अनुसार, यदि कोई संसद सदस्य सदन की अनुमति के बिना लगातार 60 दिनों तक अनुपस्थित रहता है, तो सदन उसकी सीट को रिक्त घोषित कर सकता है। यह प्रावधान लोकसभा और राज्यसभा दोनों पर लागू होता है। 60 दिनों की अवधि की गणना उस दिन से की जाती है जब से सदस्य बिना अनुमति के अनुपस्थित रहा हो। यह नियम सदस्यों की अनियमित उपस्थिति को रोकने और संसदीय कार्यप्रणाली को सुचारू बनाए रखने के लिए बनाया गया है।

question: Which charter law eliminated the East India Company's monopoly business in India? (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Charter Act 1813
Charter Act 1853
Charter Act 1833
Charter Act 1793
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Charter Act 1813

Explanation:
The Charter Act of 1813 ended the East India Company's monopoly over trade in India, except for tea and trade with China. The act renewed the Company's charter for 20 years but opened Indian trade to other British merchants. While the Company retained its political and administrative powers, the act marked a significant shift towards free trade. It also permitted Christian missionaries to operate in India and allocated funds for educational purposes. This act was passed by the British Parliament and reflected the growing influence of industrialists who opposed the Company's monopoly.

☛ Which act allowed Christian missionaries to enter India? → Charter Act 1813
☛ What sum was allocated for education by the Charter Act 1813? → 1 lakh rupees
☛ Under whose Prime Ministership was the Charter Act 1813 passed? → Lord Liverpool
question_hi: किस चार्टर कानून ने भारत में ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के एकाधिकार व्यापार को समाप्त कर दिया? (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 2)

question: What paragraph can not be suspended at the time of the emergency? (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Article 20 and Article 21
Article 22 and Article 23
Article 19 and Article 43
Article 23 and Article 24
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 20 and Article 21

Explanation:
Article 20 (Protection in respect of conviction for offences) and Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty) of the Indian Constitution cannot be suspended even during a national emergency. Article 20 ensures that no person can be punished twice for the same offence or compelled to be a witness against themselves. Article 21 guarantees that no person shall be deprived of their life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. These two articles are part of the Fundamental Rights and remain protected during an emergency. Under Article 359, the President can suspend the right to move any court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights during an emergency, but Article 20 and 21 can never be suspended. The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 further strengthened this protection. Thus, the correct answer is Article 20 and Article 21.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which articles cannot be suspended during emergency? → Article 20 and 21
☛ What does Article 20 protect? → Protection against double jeopardy and self-incrimination
☛ What is the essence of Article 21? → No deprivation of life or liberty except by procedure established by law
☛ What does Article 359 allow? → Suspension of enforcement of Fundamental Rights during emergency
☛ After which amendment are Articles 20 and 21 immune from suspension? → 44th Amendment Act, 1978
question_hi: आपातकाल के समय कौन सा अनुच्छेद निलम्बित नहीं किया जा सकता? (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 2)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 20 और अनुच्छेद 21
अनुच्छेद 22 और अनुच्छेद 23
अनुच्छेद 19 और अनुच्छेद 43
अनुच्छेद 23 और अनुच्छेद 24
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 20 और अनुच्छेद 21

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 20 (अपराधों के लिए दोषसिद्धि के संबंध में संरक्षण) और अनुच्छेद 21 (प्राण और दैहिक स्वतंत्रता का संरक्षण) को राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल के दौरान भी निलंबित नहीं किया जा सकता। अनुच्छेद 20 में कहा गया है कि किसी व्यक्ति को उसी अपराध के लिए दो बार दंडित नहीं किया जा सकता और न ही उसे स्वयं के विरुद्ध गवाही देने के लिए बाध्य किया जा सकता है। अनुच्छेद 21 के तहत किसी भी व्यक्ति को विधि द्वारा स्थापित प्रक्रिया के अलावा उसके जीवन या व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता से वंचित नहीं किया जा सकता। ये दोनों अनुच्छेद मौलिक अधिकारों की श्रेणी में आते हैं और आपातकाल के दौरान भी सुरक्षित रहते हैं। अनुच्छेद 359 के अनुसार, राष्ट्रपति आपातकाल के दौरान मौलिक अधिकारों को लागू करने के लिए किसी भी अदालत में जाने के अधिकार को निलंबित कर सकता है, लेकिन अनुच्छेद 20 और 21 को कभी निलंबित नहीं किया जा सकता।

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

question: A person who is not a member of Parliament does not belong to any House, such person can be appointed as the Prime Minister of India for a maximum period of __________. (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: 6 months 6 weeks
6 months
1 year
2 Months
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 6 months

Explanation:
According to Article 75(5) of the Indian Constitution, if a person who is not a member of either House of Parliament is appointed as Prime Minister, they must become a member of Parliament within 6 months from the date of their appointment; otherwise, they cease to hold office. This provision ensures that the Prime Minister remains accountable to the Parliament. The same rule applies to other members of the Council of Ministers as per Article 75(5). The period of 6 months is provided to maintain continuity in government functioning while ensuring democratic accountability. This constitutional requirement upholds the principle that the executive is answerable to the legislature.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which Article deals with appointment and term of ministers? → Article 75(5)
☛ How much time does a non-member minister get to become a member of Parliament? → 6 months
☛ Can the Prime Minister be a member of either House? → Yes
☛ Which Article allows a non-member to become a minister? → Article 75(5)
☛ When does the 6-month period start? → From the date of appointment
question_hi: जो व्यक्ति संसद का सदस्य नहीं है, वह किसी भी सदन से संबंधित नहीं है, ऐसे व्यक्ति को अधिकतम __________ अवधि के लिए भारत का प्रधान मंत्री नियुक्त किया जा सकता है। (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 2)

6 महीने
1 वर्ष
2 महीने
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 6 महीने

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 75(5) के अनुसार, यदि कोई व्यक्ति जो संसद का सदस्य नहीं है, उसे प्रधान मंत्री नियुक्त किया जाता है, तो उसे नियुक्ति की तारीख से 6 महीने के भीतर संसद का सदस्य बनना होता है, अन्यथा वह पद धारण नहीं कर सकता। यह प्रावधान यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि प्रधान मंत्री संसद के प्रति उत्तरदायी रहे। यह नियम मंत्रिपरिषद के अन्य सदस्यों पर भी लागू होता है, जैसा कि अनुच्छेद 75(5) में उल्लिखित है। यह अवधि सरकार के कामकाज में निरंतरता बनाए रखने और लोकतांत्रिक जवाबदेही सुनिश्चित करने के लिए निर्धारित की गई है।

question: All the representatives have been jointly elected / administered, guided and guided by the Indian Government. (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Judiciary
Chief Minister
Chief Justice of India
Parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Parliament

Explanation:
The provision described in the question pertains to the functioning of the Indian Parliament. According to the Indian Constitution, the election, administration, direction and guidance of all elected representatives in the Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) is jointly carried out by the Government of India. This process is managed through the Election Commission and other constitutional bodies. The Parliament is the supreme legislative body of India and consists of the President, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. The Judiciary, Chief Minister and Chief Justice of India are not responsible for this task. Hence, the correct answer is Parliament.

question_hi: सभी प्रतिनिधियों का निर्वाचन/प्रशासन, निर्देशन एवं मार्गदर्शन भारत सरकार द्वारा संयुक्त रूप से किया गया है। (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 2)

question: Which Act abolished the double government in India? (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Indian Independence Act of 1947
Government of India Act 1935
Government of India Act 1858
Government of India Act 1909
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act 1858

Explanation:
The Government of India Act 1858 abolished the double government in India. This act ended the Company rule and transferred the governance of India directly to the British Crown. It changed the title of Governor General to Viceroy and created the new position of Secretary of State for India. This act was enacted after the Revolt of 1857 and gave the Secretary of State authority over Indian affairs.

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1858

Explanation:

question: Which rule did the British government enforce and regulate the East India Company in India? (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Charter Act 1833
Regulating Act, 1773
Pitts India Act 1784
Government of India Act 1909
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Regulating Act, 1773

Explanation:
The British government took the first step to control the functioning of the East India Company in 1773. The Regulating Act, 1773 established government control over the company's administration. This act transformed the Governor of Bengal into the Governor-General and established a Supreme Court in Calcutta. Before this, the company was completely independent. The Charter Act of 1833 ended the company's trading rights, the Pitts India Act of 1784 introduced a dual government system, and the Government of India Act of 1909 brought the Morley-Minto reforms.

question: The first hour of each parliamentary meeting is kept for whom? (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Zero Hour
Question Hour
Privilege Hour
Whistleblower Proposal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Question Hour

Explanation:
In parliamentary democracy, the first hour of every sitting is reserved for Question Hour. During this time, members of parliament can ask questions to ministers regarding government policies and actions. The purpose of Question Hour is to hold the government accountable and ensure transparency. After Question Hour comes Zero Hour, where members can raise issues without prior notice. Privilege Hour deals with breaches of privilege of any member. Question Hour is a crucial part of parliamentary proceedings and a means of democratic control.

question: When did the Constitution of India come into force? (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: January 26, 1950
August 15, 1950
November 26, 1949
August 15, 1947
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is January 26, 1950

Explanation:
The Constitution of India came into force on January 26, 1950. This day is celebrated as Republic Day. With its enforcement, India became a sovereign republic. The Constituent Assembly had adopted the Constitution on November 26, 1949, but it was fully enforced on January 26, 1950. This date was chosen to commemorate the declaration of Purna Swaraj in 1930. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as the chairman of the Drafting Committee. At the time of enforcement, C. Rajagopalachari was the last Governor-General of India.

question: Which of the following rights is called the soul and heart of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Right to Life
Freedom of speech and expression
Right to Personal Freedom
Right to Constitutional Remedies
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right to Constitutional Remedies

Explanation:
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) the soul and heart of the Indian Constitution. This right empowers citizens to directly approach the Supreme Court or High Courts in case of violation of fundamental rights. Article 32 itself is a fundamental right, without which other fundamental rights become meaningless. Under this, writs like Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto are issued. Thus, it provides judicial protection and upholds the supremacy of the constitution.

☛ High Court → Can issue writs under Article 226

question: Which special date was selected for the implementation of the Indian Constitution?  (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019) Shift 2)

question: What is the meaning of religious freedom? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Freedom of management of religious activities; Freedom to give religious instructions to some institutions
Rights of Minorities
Equality before the law
Forced Labor Injury
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Freedom of management of religious activities; Freedom to give religious instructions to some institutions

Explanation:
Article 25 of the Indian Constitution guarantees religious freedom, including the freedom of conscience and the right to profess, practice, and propagate religion. Article 26 grants every religious denomination the right to manage its own affairs in matters of religion, establish institutions for religious and charitable purposes, and give religious instructions. These rights are subject to public order, morality, and health. The correct option combines these two freedoms: management of religious activities (from Article 26) and giving religious instructions to some institutions (related to Article 26 and 30).

question: When did the Constituent Assembly adopt the national anthem? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: 1950
1947
1988
1960
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1950

Explanation:
India's national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' was originally written in Bengali by Rabindranath Tagore. It was first sung on December 27, 1911, at the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress. The Constituent Assembly officially adopted it as the national anthem on January 24, 1950, just two days before the Constitution came into effect. The lyrics and music are both by Tagore, and the complete song lasts about 52 seconds. Rules regarding respect for the national anthem are outlined in the Indian Constitution and Supreme Court directives.

question: In which year  was the 42nd Amendment came into force to the Constitution of India? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019) Shift 2)

Explanation:

question: If the court thinks that a particular officer is not following his legal duties, in this case, what is the writ issued by the court? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Certiorari
Prohibition
Mandamus
Habeas corpus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mandamus

Explanation:
When a public officer fails to perform his legal duty, the court issues Mandamus. It is a writ that commands the officer to fulfill his duty. The literal meaning of Mandamus is 'we command'. This writ is directed to a lower court, government official, or public body. Article 32 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court, and Article 226 empowers the High Court to issue this writ. Mandamus is issued only when the duty is legal and the officer is failing to perform it. It cannot be issued against discretionary duties or private individuals.

☛ What is the literal meaning of Mandamus? → 'We command'

☛ How many writs are there in India? → Five: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo Warranto

question: In the Indian Constitution, in the case of public employment, the provision for equality of opportunity has been done for whom? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: For Foreigners
For foreigners (alien)
For all citizens
For the citizens of the neighboring country
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is For all citizens

Explanation:
Article 16 of the Indian Constitution provides equality of opportunity in matters of public employment for all citizens. It ensures that no citizen shall be disqualified or discriminated against solely on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, or residence. The state is also empowered under Article 16(4) to make reservations for backward classes. This right is restricted to Indian citizens and does not apply to foreigners or aliens. The provision aims to promote fairness and equal opportunity in the public sector, preventing arbitrary discrimination.

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान में सार्वजनिक रोजगार के मामले में अवसर की समानता का प्रावधान किसके लिए किया गया है? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019) Shift 2)

question: The concept of 'rule of law' is taken from which country's constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: British Constitution
Constitution of Australia
Ireland Constitution
American Constitution
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is British Constitution

Explanation:
The concept of 'rule of law' in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the British Constitution. This principle establishes that law is supreme and no individual is above the law. British constitutional expert A.V. Dicey clearly propounded this concept. Article 14 of the Indian Constitution, which guarantees the right to equality, is based on this principle. The rule of law ensures that the government cannot act arbitrarily and all citizens are treated equally. This concept is considered the cornerstone of a democratic system.

question: Which of the following is not part of the preamble of the Constitution of India? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Freedom
Indian Flag
Similarity
Justice
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Indian Flag

Explanation:
The Preamble of the Indian Constitution mentions Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity. These are the core objectives of the Constitution. The Indian Flag (Tricolor) is not part of the Preamble; it is a national symbol adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947. The Preamble was adopted on 26 November 1949 and reflects the philosophy and goals of the Constitution. The 42nd Amendment (1976) added the words Socialist, Secular, and Integrity to the Preamble.

question: Who is the first Muslim president of India?  (RPF Constable 2018 (19/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Mr. Muhammad Iqbal

Dr. Zakir Hussain
Dr. Manmohan Singh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dr. Zakir Hussain

Explanation:
Dr. Zakir Hussain was the first Muslim President of India. He served as President from 13 May 1967 until his death on 3 May 1969. He was a prominent educationist and politician, having served as the Vice Chancellor of Aligarh Muslim University. He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan by the Government of India. He was active in the student movement against the Nizam rule and later became a member of the Constituent Assembly of India. Dr. Zakir Hussain's term ended tragically with his death in 1969, making him the first President to die in office. His contributions to Indian education and politics are remembered to this day.

भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 75 के अनुसार, प्रधानमंत्री की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती है। प्रधानमंत्री को पद एवं गोपनीयता की शपथ राष्ट्रपति दिलाते हैं। राष्ट्रपति संघ की कार्यपालिका का प्रमुख होता है और वह प्रधानमंत्री सहित मंत्रिपरिषद के सदस्यों को शपथ ग्रहण कराता है। शपथ का प्रारूप संविधान की तीसरी अनुसूची में निर्धारित है। प्रधानमंत्री के पद की शपथ लेने के बाद ही वह अपने कर्तव्यों का पालन शुरू कर सकता है। राष्ट्रपति का यह कर्तव्य भारतीय लोकतंत्र में संवैधानिक प्रक्रिया का महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा है।
